how_we_lost: We killed ourselves: on round 13 (turn 50), The One Ring's upkeep trigger with 6 burden counters took us from 6 life to 0, heads-up against P3 (Y'shtola) at 41. The chain started on round 10, when P3's Vito plus a lifelink turn drained out P1 and P2 and put P3 at 51 while we sat at 9. Our Demonic Tutor into Pernicious Deed then wiped P3's board but also killed our own Muldrotha, because Forge chose X of 6 or more. Muldrotha's tax made her cost 10, and she never returned. From turn 42, every Claws of Gix activation meant to sacrifice the Ring sacrificed a land instead: 11 lands and then Claws itself. Meanwhile we kept tapping the Ring for cards (burden 3→6).
winnable_why: Through round 9 we were in decent shape. Muldrotha was out, Hostage Taker held Drivnod, Dellian Fel had killed Sephiroth, and The One Ring was drawing. But P3's Vito/Y'shtola engine was allowed to live, and once P3 hit 51 life with a wide board against our 9, winning needed a long heads-up grind. A strong pilot who kills Vito on round 9 and keeps Muldrotha through the Deed has a real but modest chance.

mistakes.what_happened: Heads-up on rounds 11-12, the plan was to tap The One Ring and then pay {1} on Claws of Gix to sacrifice the Ring. Each time, the sacrificed permanent was a land chosen by Forge's cost payment. On turn 42 that was Underground Sea, Hinterland Harbor, Overgrown Tomb, Tropical Island, Otawara and Boseiju. Bayou went on turn 44. Swamp, Zagoth Triome, Darkslick Shores, Breeding Pool and finally Claws itself went on turn 48. The executor overruled Forge to activate Claws again and again (6 times on turn 42) instead of stopping after the first land.
mistakes.better_play: Stop after the first wrong sacrifice. If the cost choice can't be controlled, don't build the plan on Claws. Stop tapping the Ring and let the burden stay where it is.
mistakes.why: It destroyed 11 of our lands, made Muldrotha (10 mana) impossible, and never removed the Ring that killed us.
mistakes.category: sacrifice-cost choice out of pilot control

mistakes.what_happened: After Claws had already failed to hit the Ring on turns 42 and 44, the memos still told us to tap The One Ring every turn (burden 4, 5, then 6) and 'then Claws the Ring'. On turn 46 the executor didn't activate Claws at all, although the memo called it mandatory, so the upkeep took us from 6 to 1. On turn 48 the executor tapped the Ring to burden 6 before any Ring sacrifice had worked, and we ended the turn at exactly 6 life.
mistakes.better_play: Stop tapping the Ring once a clean removal isn't guaranteed. At 1 life on turn 48, leaving the burden at 5 keeps us alive. Use the drawn cards we already had for life instead: Gray Merchant via Survival, Baba Lysaga's drain.
mistakes.why: The final Ring tap was directly lethal. The underlying error was running a life-cost card engine at single-digit life heads-up.

mistakes.what_happened: Demonic Tutor found Pernicious Deed, and the memo specified X=4 so Muldrotha (MV 6) survives. X was Forge's choice. Muldrotha died along with P3's board, Talisman and Cryogen Relic.
mistakes.better_play: Activate at X=4 or 5, which clears P3's creatures, Propaganda and Ghostly Prison while Muldrotha survives.
mistakes.why: Muldrotha's tax was already 2 after Claim the Precious, so she now cost 10. She never came back, and the heads-up game became a topdeck fight.

mistakes.what_happened: The round 9 memo said to use Dellian Fel's −3 on Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose. The executor overruled Forge's pick (the Y'shtola token copy) and aimed it at the Y'shtola commander, which went to the command zone and was recast.
mistakes.better_play: Use −3 on Vito as the memo said.
mistakes.why: On round 10, P3 made its creatures lifelink with Vito out, gained 19 and drained P1 and P2 to death. That left us heads-up against a 51-life P3. Without Vito, that turn is just an attack.

mistakes.what_happened: Heroic Intervention was cast in our main phase with nothing to protect against. The executor overruled Forge's Heroic in favor of The One Ring, then accepted it as the next action. The memo held it for a wipe or for removal on Hostage Taker or Muldrotha.
mistakes.better_play: Hold Heroic Intervention with 2 green open on opponents' turns.
mistakes.why: On turn 40 P3 Dismembered Hostage Taker. Heroic's hexproof would have fizzled that and kept the Hostage Taker line.

mistakes.what_happened: The round 3 memo said Talisman of Dominance + Baleful Strix, setting up Muldrotha on round 4. The executor cast Strix and then accepted Forge's Doc Aurlock, leaving Talisman in hand until round 6. Doc then died to Cleansing Nova.
mistakes.why: Ramp on schedule is the difference between Muldrotha on round 4 and round 5. Doc cast before Muldrotha just fed a wipe.

strategy_assessment: The memos followed the dossier's 'P2 Sephiroth is the fastest clock' and kept Y'shtola as 'slow, deal with later', but P3 is the deck that won. Vito resolved on round 7 and wasn't targeted until round 9, and the executor missed that. Mid-game plans were good: Hostage Taker on Drivnod, Fel on Sephiroth, The One Ring for cards and protection. Late-game strategy was the real failure. At 9-15 life heads-up against a drain deck, the strategist kept The One Ring as the card engine and trusted Claws of Gix to reset it after the first two attempts had eaten lands. The heads-up plan should have been life and defense first: Gray Merchant via Survival, Glen Elendra for Exsanguinate, and Baba Lysaga. Muldrotha also should have been protected through the Deed. The One Ring should have stayed untapped once its burden could not be removed.
summary: We lost to our own One Ring on round 13, heads-up against P3. We had a solid mid-game, but Vito was left alive and fueled P3's 19-point lifelink swing that killed P1 and P2. Forge's X choice on Pernicious Deed killed Muldrotha for good. Forge's Claws of Gix cost payment then sacrificed 11 lands instead of the Ring while we kept adding burden.
